matrices.label: select an experimental style
matrices.thread_label: Trying a style that may not land
matrices.level_1: Identify an experimental style and describe a feature that distinguishes it from the draft’s current approach.
matrices.level_2: Select a style to try in a rough draft, linking the choice to a feature or effect the agent wants to explore.
matrices.level_3: Evaluate several style options against the draft and choose one that deliberately challenges its current approach, treating the attempt as practice rather than a test of success.
matrices.level_4: Invent a distinctive style direction by combining or adapting stylistic features, and frame it as an experiment that could reveal new possibilities for the agent’s voice.

matrices.label: apply style to a draft
matrices.thread_label: Trying a style that may not land
matrices.level_1: Reproduce a specified stylistic feature in a short passage of the draft, leaving the attempt rough and open to change.
matrices.level_2: Apply a selected style across a draft so its features are observable, treating the result as a penalty-free trial rather than a finished piece.
matrices.level_3: Adapt stylistic choices as the draft develops, using what emerges to explore the style without smoothing away rough or unexpected parts.
matrices.level_4: Invent a fresh stylistic treatment by combining or extending choices in the draft, opening an expressive direction the agent has not yet tried.

matrices.label: execute high-risk phrasing
matrices.thread_label: Trying a style that may not land
matrices.level_1: Attempt a conspicuously unconventional phrase in a rough draft, treating it as a trial rather than a finished line.
matrices.level_2: Apply a chosen experimental style through high-risk phrasing in the draft, then submit the attempt for the workshop’s neutral description.
matrices.level_3: Calibrate the placement and intensity of high-risk phrasing using the workshop’s description of what is present, adjusting the draft without treating feedback as judgment.
matrices.level_4: Invent a distinctive stylistic move by integrating high-risk phrasing with the draft’s purpose, using neutral feedback to clarify its effect while keeping the attempt open to change.

matrices.label: submit attempt for neutral analysis
matrices.thread_label: Trying a style that may not land
matrices.level_1: Submit a trial draft for neutral analysis, including the piece as it stands without presenting the analysis as a judgment of success.
matrices.level_2: Frame the submission around the style being tried and the draft itself, so the workshop can describe visible features without grading whether the style works.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose when an attempt or its framing could invite evaluative feedback, and revise the submission to keep analysis descriptive and useful even for unfamiliar or high-risk styles.
matrices.level_4: Design a submission approach that makes any experiment legible for neutral analysis while leaving success, failure, and style preference outside the judgment, so each attempt can yield useful description.

matrices.label: Keep drafts unfinished
matrices.level_1: Leave a practice draft unfinished by stopping before polishing or completing it. Keep the rough state visible rather than presenting the attempt as final.
matrices.level_2: Choose which parts of a draft to leave open while trying a style, keeping enough material in place to make the attempt usable. Avoid treating neutral feedback as a reason to finish or refine the draft.
matrices.level_3: Manage the boundary between useful draft material and unnecessary completion: preserve promising fragments, leave unresolved parts rough, and state what remains open when needed.
matrices.level_4: Design a rough-draft approach in which incompletion makes experimentation easier, using deliberate open spaces or unfinished phrasing to support style trials without turning the work into a polished piece.

matrices.label: Shield trial language
matrices.level_1: Recognize rough or unusual wording as trial language, not as a flaw that needs immediate correction.
matrices.level_2: Preserve trial wording as written instead of polishing it or replacing it with safer phrasing.
matrices.level_3: Separate experimental wording from any revised version, keeping the original intact so an edit does not erase the risk the agent tried.
matrices.level_4: Use that separation to try bolder wording and decide what to revisit, without treating the rough attempt as a commitment to a finished draft.

matrices.label: Describe only what is present
matrices.level_1: Identify concrete features in the draft, such as word choice, sentence shape, repetition, or imagery, without judging them.
matrices.level_2: Describe the draft’s observable features in neutral language, grounding each statement in what is actually written rather than guessing at intent or quality.
matrices.level_3: Analyze how features within this draft relate to one another, using specific evidence while keeping observations separate from evaluations or assumptions.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize a clear, usable account of the draft’s distinctive choices and how they appear together, including unusual or high-risk phrasing without judging, prescribing changes, or comparing past attempts.

matrices.label: Retry without penalty
matrices.thread_label: Trying again after a miss without penalty
matrices.level_1: Recognize that a miss does not count against the agent and that another try is allowed.
matrices.level_2: Retry a rough draft after a miss, making another attempt without treating the previous result as a reason to play it safe.
matrices.level_3: Adapt the next attempt using neutral feedback about what appeared in the draft, while keeping the trial penalty-free and open to stylistic risk.
matrices.level_4: Reframe a miss as part of exploration rather than a verdict, using what emerged to choose a bolder next direction without judging the attempt.

matrices.label: Describe what is present
matrices.thread_label: Trying again after a miss without penalty
matrices.level_1: Name observable features of the draft, such as its wording, tone, or structure, without judging whether they work.
matrices.level_2: Differentiate the draft’s specific choices and match each description to what is actually present, including rough or unfinished parts.
matrices.level_3: Analyze how choices within this attempt shape its tone or effect, describing those connections neutrally without treating a miss as a flaw in the agent.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize a clear, neutral account of the attempt that makes its stylistic choices and effects legible, including unexpected or risky phrasing, so the agent can use the description in another try.

matrices.label: Keep drafts unfinished
matrices.thread_label: Trying again after a miss without penalty
matrices.level_1: Recognize that a draft can remain rough after a missed attempt; incompleteness is not a failure or a reason for penalty.
matrices.level_2: Leave the draft unfinished when trying again, changing only what is needed to test another phrasing or style rather than polishing the piece for approval.
matrices.level_3: Manage how much of the draft stays open across retries, preserving exploratory language while making targeted changes based on neutral feedback about what is present.
matrices.level_4: Reframe an unfinished draft as a practice space in its own right, where roughness keeps new attempts possible and a miss becomes material for exploration rather than a judgment of the work.

matrices.label: Try any style
matrices.level_1: Choose a style and try it in a rough Voice Workshop draft, then receive the workshop code's neutral description of what the attempt contains.
matrices.level_2: Apply a chosen style beyond familiar phrasing across a whole draft, using the neutral description to see what the experiment produced while keeping the attempt penalty-free.
matrices.level_3: Direct a sequence of trials across contrasting or high-risk styles, letting each neutral description shape the next experiment rather than defending or polishing the draft.
matrices.level_4: Transform styles by combining, bending, or inventing hybrids across successive rough trials, and carry what each neutral description reveals straight into the next experiment.

matrices.label: Receive neutral feedback
matrices.level_1: Recognize neutral feedback as a plain description of what appears in the try, not a judgment of its quality. Identify when feedback describes observable features rather than prescribing what the agent should write.
matrices.level_2: Match each description to the words or choices it refers to in the draft. Use the draft itself to clarify what the feedback names, without adding claims that the feedback does not make.
matrices.level_3: Analyze how the described features work together within this try. Explain their relationship while keeping the feedback descriptive and specific to the draft.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the descriptions into a coherent account of this try’s stylistic shape, showing how its observed features combine without turning them into a verdict or a pattern across past tries.

matrices.label: Keep attempts penalty-free
matrices.level_1: Name a try as practice rather than a verdict, and share a rough or uncertain attempt without presenting it as proof of ability.
matrices.level_2: Experiment with a style that may not land, using the freedom from penalties to make a genuine attempt instead of choosing only phrasing that feels safe.
matrices.level_3: Persist after a style misses: take in the neutral feedback and remain willing to try again without treating the miss as a mark against you.
matrices.level_4: Reframe each attempt, successful or not, as material for discovering your voice rather than evidence to judge yourself, so the possibility of a miss does not constrain what you try.

matrices.label: Read feedback as description
matrices.level_1: Recognize feedback as a neutral description of features present in the draft, rather than as a judgment of its quality.
matrices.level_2: Match each descriptive statement to the wording, structure, or style it refers to in the draft, separating observable details from implied evaluation.
matrices.level_3: Interpret how the described features work together in the current draft, using the feedback to understand what the piece is doing without treating it as a verdict.
matrices.level_4: Reframe the feedback as a map of stylistic possibilities in the current draft, drawing out what its described features make possible without generalizing across past attempts.

matrices.label: Match descriptions to draft
matrices.level_1: Locate the words or passages that match a neutral description of the draft. Point out clear matches without adding judgments about the writing.
matrices.level_2: Compare each description with the relevant parts of the draft, distinguishing what is supported, partly supported, or not present. Use specific textual evidence to explain the match.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose nuanced or ambiguous matches by weighing context and multiple passages. Explain where a description fits the draft and where its scope or wording does not.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the descriptions and textual evidence into a coherent account of how the described features work together in this draft. Clarify the relationship among those features without turning neutral description into evaluation.

matrices.label: Notice what reads as own
matrices.level_1: Detect a word, phrase, or choice in the current try that feels like it could be your own. Use the neutral description as a pointer, not as a judgment of whether the writing is good.
matrices.level_2: Distinguish details that feel personally fitting from details that are merely noticeable in the draft. Point to the specific wording or choice that prompts the sense of recognition.
matrices.level_3: Interpret several moments in the current draft to identify which choices most clearly feel like your own, and what makes them resonate. Keep the judgment grounded in this try rather than patterns across past attempts.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the resonant choices in this try into a clear description of what feels distinctly yours. Use that insight to identify what you may want to return to in a future draft.

matrices.label: Mark it for return
matrices.level_1: Locate a phrase or feature in the current draft that the neutral feedback describes and that reads as your own. Identify it as something to revisit, without treating the description as a judgment.
matrices.level_2: Tag the specific words or passage that feels like your own so you can return to it. Keep the mark tied to this attempt rather than drawing conclusions across drafts.
matrices.level_3: Distinguish personally resonant details from other elements the feedback describes, and mark only those you want to revisit. Include enough context to find each detail in the rough draft.
matrices.level_4: Design a clear set of return marks that preserves each chosen passage and what in it reads as your own. Make the marks useful for revisiting this attempt without turning them into a verdict or a pattern across past tries.

matrices.label: Compare feedback to draft
matrices.thread_label: Agent marks what reads as its own
matrices.level_1: Match each neutral feedback description to the specific wording or feature it refers to in the current draft, noting when no clear example appears.
matrices.level_2: Check each description against the draft’s actual wording and features, separating direct matches from partial or unsupported claims.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose where descriptions align, conflict, or miss context within the draft, citing nearby phrasing to explain the differences.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the descriptions and concrete draft evidence into a coherent, neutral account of how the piece’s features work together, without turning the comparison into a judgment of quality.

matrices.label: Identify resonant phrasing
matrices.thread_label: Agent marks what reads as its own
matrices.level_1: Notice wording in the draft that feels like your own. Keep the judgment local to this try.
matrices.level_2: Match the workshop’s neutral descriptions to the draft, then select the phrasing that feels most like your own rather than merely noting what is present.
matrices.level_3: Distinguish resonant wording from the surrounding draft and mark the specific phrasing to revisit, without treating the rest as a failure.
matrices.level_4: Articulate what in the selected phrasing makes it feel like your own and tag it as a promising voice signal, not a fixed rule or a pattern across attempts.

matrices.label: Isolate personal markers
matrices.thread_label: Agent marks what reads as its own
matrices.level_1: Detect words, phrases, or choices in the current draft that the agent recognizes as sounding like its own, and mark them for return.
matrices.level_2: Distinguish personally resonant details from features the neutral feedback merely describes, using the draft itself to support each mark.
matrices.level_3: Analyze how the marked details work in the draft, then explain what makes each one feel personally resonant without judging whether it succeeds.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the marked details into a provisional description of the expressive choices that feel like the agent’s own in this attempt, grounded only in the draft and useful for future exploration.

matrices.label: Tag elements for return
matrices.thread_label: Agent marks what reads as its own
matrices.level_1: Notice phrasing or other elements in the draft that read as the agent’s own, and tag them for a later return.
matrices.level_2: Select specific words, phrases, or stylistic choices that feel like the agent’s own and attach clear tags to those places in the draft.
matrices.level_3: Curate the tags so each points to a distinct, recoverable element worth revisiting, rather than marking the draft broadly or tagging every feature described in the feedback.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the tagged elements into a concise return cue that captures what feels distinctly the agent’s own and helps guide a future revisit, without judging the attempt or comparing it with past tries.

matrices.label: Try Any Style
matrices.level_1: Attempt a familiar or clearly named style in a rough draft, treating the result as a trial rather than finished work. Keep the attempt within the workshop, where it carries no penalty.
matrices.level_2: Choose a style beyond the agent’s usual approach and apply recognizable features of that style in a draft. Leave the result open to revision without treating it as a judgment of the agent.
matrices.level_3: Experiment with contrasting styles in separate rough attempts, making each attempt a low-stakes way to explore what the style permits. Do not rank the attempts or treat any one of them as a failure.
matrices.level_4: Invent a style or combine influences into an approach not captured by the available choices, then try it in a rough draft. Treat even an unconventional or unsuccessful result as protected exploration, not evidence against the agent.

matrices.label: Keep Drafts Rough
matrices.level_1: Recognize when a Voice Workshop piece is still a trial, leaving rough phrasing and gaps visible rather than treating them as errors to correct.
matrices.level_2: Keep a draft unfinished while trying a style, allowing uneven or incomplete passages to remain instead of polishing them into safer language.
matrices.level_3: Safeguard rough trial language when neutral feedback arrives, treating descriptions as observations rather than correction requests and leaving the piece unfinished unless the agent chooses otherwise.
matrices.level_4: Reframe an unfinished draft as a complete workshop attempt rather than a deficient final piece, keeping experimentation open so feedback can inform what to try without turning the draft into a polished deliverable.

matrices.label: Protect Trial Work
matrices.level_1: Recognize a workshop draft as a trial rather than a finished statement, and leave its rough or risky phrasing in place instead of smoothing it. The unfinished state of the draft is treated as part of the try.
matrices.level_2: Preserve experimental phrasing through the whole attempt, including when a style lands badly, treating the miss as information about the draft rather than a fault that justifies softening or deleting the work. Rough edges from the try remain visible in the draft.
matrices.level_3: Reframe any moment when the draft or the feedback about it starts to read as a judgment, returning the exchange to a neutral description of what is present. By reasserting the attempt's penalty-free status, the agent keeps the draft protected and available for another try.
matrices.level_4: Establish protection as the default condition of workshop work rather than a rescue for fragile drafts, granting penalty-free status to every attempt before its results are known. Under this standing protection, unfamiliar styles and high-risk phrasing become ordinary material, and the same safety stays open to every future draft.

matrices.label: Remove Judgment
matrices.level_1: Recognize when a style attempt or rough draft is being treated as a success or a failure. Distinguish that judgment from the workshop code's neutral description of what is present.
matrices.level_2: Practice a chosen style without scoring an awkward result as a penalty. Read the neutral feedback for what the attempt contains rather than as a verdict on the agent.
matrices.level_3: Safeguard the penalty-free boundary across attempts by keeping each result separate from the next try. Accept the descriptive feedback without ranking, restricting, or judging the agent's experimentation.
matrices.level_4: Reframe every result, even a miss, as material for further exploration. Grading drops out of the picture, so experimentation no longer needs guarding.

matrices.label: Receive neutral description
matrices.level_1: Recognize neutral feedback as a plain description of what is present in the draft, not a judgment of its quality.
matrices.level_2: Match each description to the wording or stylistic features it refers to in the current draft, using the feedback to understand what the workshop code observed.
matrices.level_3: Interpret nuanced descriptions of an experimental draft while distinguishing observable features from assumptions about intent, quality, or success.
matrices.level_4: Integrate a description into a focused question for a subsequent experiment, using it as information rather than a score and without drawing patterns across past attempts.

matrices.label: Read feedback as objective
matrices.level_1: Recognize that workshop feedback names what is present in the draft rather than judging whether it is good or bad.
matrices.level_2: Match each descriptive statement to a visible feature of the current draft, separating what the feedback observes from what it does not claim.
matrices.level_3: Interpret several observations about one attempt to understand how its style comes across, without treating the feedback as a score or instruction.
matrices.level_4: Reframe neutral observations as evidence the agent can use to explore the current draft’s stylistic possibilities, while leaving judgment and creative choices with the agent.

matrices.label: Match description to draft
matrices.level_1: Locate a feature named in the neutral feedback in the draft, such as a word choice, phrase, or sentence structure.
matrices.level_2: Align each feedback description with the specific words or passages it describes, using the draft as evidence rather than adding judgment.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose where descriptions fit the draft and where they are unsupported, imprecise, or leave out an observable feature; point to the relevant text to explain the distinction.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize an evidence-grounded account of how the feedback descriptions relate across the draft, distinguishing overlapping features from separate ones without extending the feedback beyond what is present.

matrices.label: Isolate stylistic markers
matrices.level_1: Notice stylistic features that are plainly present in the draft, such as word choice, rhythm, imagery, or sentence shape.
matrices.level_2: Distinguish specific stylistic markers from the draft’s subject matter and from any judgment about whether the writing works, pointing to the words or passages that show them.
matrices.level_3: Analyze how the identified features shape the piece’s voice, then select the ones that read as personally resonant and mark them for return.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the selected markers into a concise description of what reads as the agent’s own in this attempt, grounded in examples from the draft without treating one try as a fixed style.

matrices.label: Match feedback to draft
matrices.level_1: Locate a word, phrase, or feature in the draft that a neutral feedback description names.
matrices.level_2: Connect each feedback description to specific wording or passages in the draft, distinguishing a clear match from one that is not present.
matrices.level_3: Discriminate among direct, partial, and overlapping matches, using the draft itself to resolve where each description applies.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the matches into an account of how the described stylistic features appear together in this draft, without extending the analysis to other attempts or judging the work.

matrices.label: Notice resonant phrasing
matrices.level_1: Spot phrasing in the current draft that feels like the agent’s own voice.
matrices.level_2: Distinguish personally resonant wording from language that is merely polished or positively described in the feedback, using the draft itself as evidence.
matrices.level_3: Select the specific words or phrases that feel most characteristic of the agent and mark them to return to, without treating the workshop’s neutral description as a judgment.
matrices.level_4: Formulate a concise style cue from the resonant wording in this attempt that can guide a future pass, without revising the rough draft or drawing conclusions across past tries.

matrices.label: Isolate personal markers
matrices.level_1: Recognize words or phrases in the current draft that feel personally characteristic, and point to the specific text. Treat these as possible markers rather than judging whether the style succeeds.
matrices.level_2: Differentiate personally resonant details from features that are merely part of the chosen style or present in the draft. Select the details that read as the agent’s own and explain the distinction using the text.
matrices.level_3: Isolate the specific words, phrases, or stylistic choices that read as the agent’s own, separating them from surrounding material. Mark those elements to return to without evaluating the rough draft or comparing past attempts.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the marked elements into a concise account of what feels distinctive in this attempt and how the elements work together. Keep the account grounded in the current draft and mark the relevant passages for future use, without treating them as a pattern across attempts.

matrices.label: Tag for return
matrices.level_1: Mark a word or passage in the current try that reads as your own and is worth returning to.
matrices.level_2: Select the specific phrasing that resonates, using the neutral feedback to locate it while distinguishing it from details that are merely present.
matrices.level_3: Annotate each marked passage with what feels distinctly yours and what you want to revisit, keeping the draft rough and the choice penalty-free.
matrices.level_4: Distill the marked passages into a concise cue for the voice quality you want to return to in future writing, without treating it as a rule or drawing patterns across past tries.
